hypothesis: For large inputs, reducing 2,048 input values per 256-thread block with CUB BlockReduce should produce a compact partial array, allowing one final BlockReduce kernel to replace repeated reduction passes and a separate copy. For inputs that fit one tile, a single BlockReduce kernel can write directly to out. These are performance hypotheses only; the candidate has not been measured.
notes: The supplied baseline is valid with a mean of 46.48 µs (baseline-e1); no candidate result is available yet. The implementation uses only provided scratch for multi-block partials and relies on ordered default-stream kernel launches. Correctness and performance remain for controller evaluation.
transformations: Replace repeated shared-memory reduction passes with cub::BlockReduce<int, 256> in each input tile.
Assign each thread eight strided items, with bounds checks, to cover a 2,048-element tile and emit one partial per block.
For inputs larger than one tile, reduce partials in a single CUB BlockReduce kernel and write directly to out.
For inputs fitting one tile, use one BlockReduce kernel to write directly to out without scratch or a second launch.
Use no device-wide CUB API, custom warp/block collective, or scratch beyond the provided partial buffer.
